slot.brief: Give the trajectory equation y = ax − bx² of a projectile and ask the student to extract the launch speed and angle of projection by matching with the standard form; possibly combine with range or max-height extraction.

stem: A projectile has trajectory $y=\dfrac34x-\dfrac{5}{64}x^2$, with $x$ and $y$ measured in metres. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, its launch speed, projection angle and horizontal range are:

verdicts.working: Comparing coefficients gives tanθ = 3/4 and g/(2u² cos²θ) = 5/64. With cos²θ = 16/25 and g = 10, u = 10 m s⁻¹. The nonzero root of y = 0 is x = 48/5 m.

working:
$a=\dfrac34=\tan\theta\Rightarrow\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{16}{25}$; $b=\dfrac{5}{64}=\dfrac{g}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}\Rightarrow u^2=100$; $u=10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$; $R=\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{48}{5}\ \text{m}$.

Independent check: Comparing coefficients gives tanθ = 3/4 and g/(2u² cos²θ) = 5/64. With cos²θ = 16/25 and g = 10, u = 10 m s⁻¹. The nonzero root of y = 0 is x = 48/5 m.
solution: For a projectile, $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{g x^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$. Comparing coefficients gives $\tan\theta=\dfrac34$ and $\dfrac{10}{2u^2(16/25)}=\dfrac{5}{64}$, hence $u=10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The range is the nonzero root of $y=0$: $R=\dfrac{3/4}{5/64}=\dfrac{48}{5}\ \text{m}$.
